description: The plot illustrates how ACC (%) varies with Co-occurrence Number for multiple methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, a purple-series method with a partially obscured legend label, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from about 1 to about 3000, with major ticks shown at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging roughly from 25% to 60%, with labeled ticks at 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, and 55. The Base line is black with circular markers and a solid line, increasing from about 28% at the smallest co-occurrence value to about 31% around ~30, reaching about 32% around ~300, and staying near ~32% at the largest value. The FT line is blue with downward-triangle markers and a solid line, rising from about 32% to about 36% (~30), then to about 37% (~300), and ending near about 38% at the largest value. The IKE line is red with upward-triangle markers and a solid line, increasing from about 33% to about 38% (~30), then to about 39–40% (~300), and ending near about 41–42%. The MEND line is brown with diamond markers and a solid line, moving from about 36–37% to about 41% (~30), then to about 45% (~300), and ending near about 45–46%. The purple line (legend label obscured) uses pentagon-like markers with a solid line, starting near about 36%, rising to about 43% (~30), then to about 46% (~300), and ending near about 46–47%. The ROME line is green with square markers and a solid line, increasing from about 44% to about 49% (~30), then to about 56% (~300), and ending near about 58–59% at the largest co-occurrence value.
